Flag.d: An option you add to a command to change how it behaves, written with one dash and a letter (-p) or two dashes and a word (--print). Some flags take a value, such as --model opus.

Subcommand.d: A word after a program's name that selects a separate job it can do, such as the 'mcp' in 'claude mcp list' or the 'commit' in 'git commit'.

Exit code.d: A number a command returns when it finishes: 0 usually means success, anything else means some kind of failure. Scripts and CI pipelines check it to decide what to do next.

Git worktree.d: An extra working copy of the same git repository, in its own folder and on its own branch, so separate tasks can change files without getting in each other's way.

Print mode.d: Running Claude Code with -p (--print): it answers once, prints the result and exits instead of opening a conversation. Used in scripts and CI pipelines.
